newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Amgen off, IBM up.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Amgen off, IBM up.

text.p: Shares of Amgen Inc were trading lower in the U.S. pre-open at 59-7/8 from Tuesday's 61-5/8 close after Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock to outperform from strong buy, traders said.
Meanwhile, International Business Machines Corp was trading higher at 114 from Tuesday's 111-3/4 finish. Traders saw no specific reasons for the stock rise.
"Somebody must have decided it's time to buy" IBM shares, said Soundview Financial computer analyst Gary Helmig. "There's no news."

In other activity ahead of the market opening, Philip Morris Cos Inc continued to rebound and was trading at 92-3/4 from Tuesday's 91-7/8 finish. Traders said shares were bolstered by hopes of a dividend increase and stock split. Morris' board of directors is meeting today.
First Team Sports Inc was trading at 8-7/8, down from Tuesday's 9-3/4 close after forecasting "significantly lower" second-quarter sales and earnings.
Archer Daniels Midland Co shares slipped 3/8 to 18 in London but were not trading in the U.S. pre-open.

On Tuesday, three foreign firms agreed to deals with the U.S. government, settling charges that they conspired to fix prices for lysine, an animal feed supplement. Archer Daniels remains a key target of the investigation in the lysine case.

Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said the latest development in the lysine case could hurt Archer Daniel but shares are already trading at very low multiple so damage is likely to be limited."
